creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Opening a window onto a zoomed tab draws the tab unzoomed for about 110ms before
settling back. herdr's bootstrap replay walks the tab backwards through the
arrangements it has had, and one of those is the tab before it was zoomed.
`arranges` (`crates/muster-core/src/composition/view.rs`) withholds a tree that
disagrees with the tab's pane list, but a stale *unzoomed* tree names exactly the
panes the tab holds, so it passes and the window draws it.

## The trace

From a run opening onto a tab of four panes with one zoomed:

    41.968  view.region  tree=p21bz8s7e7*                     <- zoomed, one pane
    42.180  channel.listening x1, tree=(not yet published)
    42.290  channel.listening x1, tree=(not yet published)
    42.399  channel.listening x1, tree=rows(rows(rows(4 panes)))  <- stale, unzoomed
    42.508  view.region  tree=p21bz8s7e7*                     <- zoomed again

## How it was found

`a_2J1KZe2ws`, the false deaf-pane alarm on a zoomed tab. Narrowing `open_channels`
to the panes the view names took the sockets bound before the first view from four to
one, and the alarm came back anyway: at 42.399 the window really is drawing all four
panes, so three more sockets bind correctly and then outlive the drawing. The alarm is
what made this visible, and fixing the alarm hides it again.

## The question

Whether `arranges` should reject a replayed arrangement that disagrees with the
region's zoom, the way it already rejects one that disagrees with the tab's pane list.
The pane set is not enough to tell a current arrangement from a stale one when the
only difference is the zoom.

Worth knowing before deciding: the card that found this did not hit the flash in its
own reproduction, where the replay never produced an unzoomed tree that passed
`arranges`. So this fires on some launches and not others, and what decides it is not
established.
title: 🫨 A launch onto a zoomed tab flashes the unzoomed layout for ~110ms
